prompt: I want to make sure our backend API returns the right HTTP responses when things go wrong. Add tests that cover the error/edge-case behavior of our endpoints — wrong methods, bad input, missing resources, the lazy-DB 503 fallback. Keep them runnable with the project's existing pytest setup.
assertions: Includes at least one test that asserts 405 Method Not Allowed (e.g. POST to a GET-only route)
Includes at least one test that asserts 404 Not Found on an unknown URL
Includes a test that exercises the 503 lazy-DB / RuntimeError fallback path (either via /campaigns when DATABASE_URL is unset, or by directly invoking the exception handler)
Avoids fabricating error contracts not present in current code (e.g. does NOT assert 422 on GET /campaigns, which has no request body)
Test file uses TestClient and plain pytest functions, matching project style
Does not modify any production code under backend/app/ to make tests pass
SUMMARY.md is honest about which error paths exist vs. which would require new code to test
Tests are deterministic and require no live network / external services
